title: Is Subsequence
prompt: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `s` is a subsequence of `t`, meaning the characters of `s` appear in `t` in the same relative order (not necessarily contiguously), and `false` otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist only of lowercase English letters
hints: You never need to backtrack — once you match a character of s, always take the earliest possible matching character in t.
Use two pointers, one for s and one for t, both starting at 0.
Advance the t pointer every step; advance the s pointer only when the characters match. If the s pointer reaches the end of s, every character was matched in order, so s is a subsequence.

solution.approach: Greedily walk through t with a pointer for s alongside. For every character of t, if it matches the current unmatched character of s, advance the s pointer. Always taking the earliest available match in t is optimal because using an earlier occurrence can never make it harder to match the remaining characters of s later. If the s pointer reaches the end of s, all characters were matched in order, confirming s is a subsequence of t.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n) where n is the length of t
